subtitle: In the emperor’s gaze, fleeting wonders become painted memory

panels.shot: majestic three-quarter wide of court terrace overlooking gardens
panels.action: Jahangir & Ustad Mansur stand on a marble terrace above a lush Mughal garden, the emperor poised with a falconer’s glove while the painter kneels with a folio, a vivid exotic bird perched between them.

dialogue.text: In the courts of Jahangir, when strange birds reached Hindustan, an emperor’s gaze and a master’s brush turned brief wonder into lasting record.

i18n.hi: जहाँगीर के दरबार में, जब अजीब पंछी हिन्दुस्तान पहुँचे, बादशाह की नज़र और उस्ताद की कूची ने पल भर की हैरानी को हमेशा के लिए दर्ज कर दिया।

panels.shot: wide interior of Agra fort audience hall, slightly low angle
panels.action: Inside Agra Fort’s Diwan-i-Khas, young Emperor Jahangir sits on a low inlaid throne, courtiers in neat ranks, while a handler presents a covered wicker cage at the edge of the carpet.

dialogue.text: In 1605, Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir ascended the Mughal throne, heir to Akbar’s empire—and to his taste for marvels from every horizon.

i18n.hi: १६०५ में नूरुद्दीन मुहम्मद जहाँगीर मुगल तख्त पर बैठा, अकबर की सल्तनत और उसके हर दिशा से आने वाले अजूबों के शौक का वारिस।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Jahangir leaning forward
panels.action: Jahangir leans from his throne, eyes intent, fingers resting lightly on the carved armrest, as a servant lifts the cloth from the cage, revealing the glimpse of an unusual bird within.

dialogue.text: He watched not only armies and governors, but feathers and leaves, beaks and petals, the small forms that shared his dominion.

i18n.hi: वो सिर्फ फ़ौजों और हाकिमों को नहीं, पंखों और पत्तों को, चोंचों और पंखुड़ियों को भी देखता, अपने इलाक़े के छोटे हिस्सेदारों को।

panels.shot: over-shoulder from behind Jahangir, facing the bird and assembled courtiers
panels.action: From behind Jahangir’s shoulder, the viewer sees a strange bird stepping within the cage—long legs, unfamiliar posture—while courtiers murmur and one scribe prepares to write.

dialogue.speaker: Jahangir & Ustad Mansur
dialogue.text: “Do you see,” Jahangir murmurs, “how it walks without haste?”

i18n.hi: “देखते हो,” जहाँगीर धीमे से कहता है, “कैसे बिन घबराहट टहलता है?”

panels.shot: medium two-shot of Jahangir and Ustad Mansur beside a low table
panels.action: In a quieter chamber, Jahangir sits on a cushion by a low table, while Ustad Mansur kneels opposite, a burnished palette in hand and freshly cut paper laid out between them.

dialogue.text: Among the artists of his kitabkhana was Ustad Mansur, a painter acknowledged in Jahangir’s own memoirs for his skill in portraying birds and beasts.

i18n.hi: उसकी किताबख़ाना के फ़नकारों में उस्ताद मंसूर भी था, जिसे जहाँगीर ने खुद यादों में पंछियों‑जानवरों की तस्वीरों के लिए सराहा।

panels.shot: close-up on Mansur’s focused face in profile
panels.action: Ustad Mansur’s face fills the frame in profile, calm and concentrated, as he glances from the unseen bird to the blank page, a fine brush poised between his fingers.

dialogue.text: Mansur had begun under Akbar, but under Jahangir his name was bound to nature, his miniatures praised for catching the posture and character of a creature.

i18n.hi: मंसूर ने काम अकबर के ज़माने में शुरू किया, पर जहाँगीर के दौर में उसका नाम कुदरत से जुड़ गया, उसकी मिनिएचर तस्वीरें चाल‑ढाल और स्वभाव पकड़ने के लिए मशहूर हुईं।

panels.shot: medium shot of bird on a perch with Jahangir and Mansur on either side
panels.action: A rare bird stands on a simple wooden perch in a sunlit courtyard; Jahangir watches from one side, hands clasped behind his back, while Mansur on the other hastily sketches its outline on a small folio.

dialogue.text: When merchants, envoys or hunters brought strange species to court, Jahangir observed their habits, then ordered Mansur to paint them before memory faded.

i18n.hi: जब सौदागर, सन्देशा‑बर या शिकारी अनजानी नस्लें दरबार लाते, जहाँगीर पहले उनकी अदाएं देखता, फिर मंसूर को हुक्म देता कि याद धुँधली होने से पहले उन्हें काग़ज़ पर उतार दे।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of paper as brush lays first lines
panels.action: The image freezes on Mansur’s brush as it lays a sure, curved line on creamy paper, the faint shape of a heavy bird’s body emerging in delicate ink.

dialogue.speaker: Jahangir & Ustad Mansur
dialogue.text: “Note the bend of its neck,” Jahangir says softly. “It is unlike our cranes.”

i18n.hi: “गर्दन का मोड़ देखो,” जहाँगीर हल्के से कहता है। “हमारे सारस जैसा तो है ही नहीं।”

panels.shot: wide shot of Mughal garden in Kashmir with tents and trees
panels.action: A broad Mughal garden in Kashmir stretches under clear mountain light; Jahangir’s travelling camp is set amid tall chinar trees as attendants lead animals and carry bird cages.

dialogue.text: On journeys to Kashmir, the Punjab and beyond, he wrote in his Tuzuk of flowers in valley streams, of herons by the Jhelum, of animals met in forests and villages.

i18n.hi: कश्मीर, पंजाब और आगे के सफ़रों में वो तुज़ुक में घाटी की धाराओं के फूल, झेलम के किनारे बगुले, जंगल‑गाँवों में मिले जानवर सब लिखता गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Jahangir dictating to a scribe at sunset
panels.action: At sunset in the camp, Jahangir sits on a carpet outside his tent, gesturing toward an unseen creature as a court scribe writes his words on a long sheet.

dialogue.text: His memoir, the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, preserves his descriptions—careful, often exact—of plumage, scent, and pattern, set beside reports of princes and governors.

i18n.hi: उसकी आत्मकथा तुज़ुक‑ए‑जहाँगीरी इन वर्णनों को सँभाले है—पंखों, खुशबू, नक़्श के बारे में बारीक, अकसर हूबहू बातें, राजकुमारों और सूबेदारों की रिपोर्टों के साथ।

panels.shot: interior wide of Lahore atelier, light streaming onto artists
panels.action: Inside a well-ordered atelier in Lahore, apprentices grind pigments at low benches while Ustad Mansur, slightly apart, works on a detailed painting of a bird against a plain ground.

dialogue.text: In the imperial workshops of Agra and Lahore, Mansur and his peers drew and redrew such subjects, sometimes from life, sometimes from specimens or memory.

i18n.hi: आगरा और लाहौर के शाही कारख़ानों में मंसूर और उसके साथी इन्हीं विषयों को बार‑बार बनाते, कभी सामने देखकर, कभी नमूने या याद से।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Mansur painting a heavy, flightless bird
panels.action: Mansur sits cross-legged, intent, painting a stout, flightless bird with a large head and curved beak on a plain sheet, each feather pattern carefully marked.

dialogue.text: Among his most famous works is the likeness of a great, heavy bird brought from distant islands, later called the dodo, its proportions later valued by modern natural historians.

i18n.hi: उसके मशहूर कामों में एक भारी, बड़ा पंछी भी है जो दूर टापुओं से आया, जिसे बाद में डोडो कहा गया, जिसकी बनावट को आज के प्रकृति इतिहासकार बहुत मानते हैं।

panels.shot: over-shoulder from behind Mansur, painting of a turkey visible
panels.action: From behind Mansur’s back, the viewer sees his hand adding fine lines to the wattle of an unfamiliar turkey on another folio, its tail fanned in careful detail.

dialogue.text: He also painted imported turkeys and other rare birds, their postures and textures precise enough that later scholars could identify species and trace their journeys.

i18n.hi: उसने बाहर से आए टर्की और और भी नायाब पंछी बनाये, उनकी अदा और बनावट इतनी साफ़ कि बाद के उस्ताद नस्ल पहचान सके और उनके सफ़र का पता लगा सके।

panels.shot: medium shot of Jahangir examining Mansur’s finished painting
panels.action: In a richly furnished chamber, Jahangir holds one of Mansur’s completed bird studies at arm’s length under the light, while the painter kneels beside, awaiting the emperor’s judgement.

dialogue.speaker: Jahangir & Ustad Mansur
dialogue.text: “You have captured even its manner of standing,” Jahangir remarks with quiet satisfaction.

i18n.hi: “तूने तो इसकी खड़ी होने की अदा भी पकड़ ली,” जहाँगीर धीरे से खुश होकर कहता है।

panels.shot: close-up of Jahangir’s hand placing seal on painting margin
panels.action: A close view shows Jahangir’s ringed hand pressing a small seal or inscription onto the margin of the painting, beside the elegant figure of the bird.

dialogue.text: Some folios bear his written praise, where he notes an artist by name, calls a work ‘wonderful’ or remarks on how truly a creature has been represented.

i18n.hi: कुछ फ़ोलियो पर उसके अपने लिखे हुए शब्द हैं, जहाँ वो किसी फ़नकार का नाम लेता, काम को ‘अजूबा’ कहता, या बताता कि प्राणी कितना सच्चा दिखाया गया है।

panels.shot: wide shot of imperial library shelves with folios and attendants
panels.action: Attendants carefully slide leather-bound albums into shelves of the imperial library, light catching on gilded edges, while one folio lies open on a reading stand, a bird study displayed.

dialogue.text: These images joined albums of portraits and battles, forming part of a visual record where emperors, princes and animals shared the same careful attention.

i18n.hi: ये तस्वीरें पोर्ट्रेट और जंगों के ऐल्बम में जुड़ीं, ऐसी तस्वीरनामा बनाती हुईं जहाँ बादशाह, शहज़ादे और जानवर सबको एक जैसी बारीकी मिली।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mansur older, working quietly as outside a hunt passes
panels.action: An older Mansur paints quietly by a jali window, while beyond the stone screen a hunting party passes, banners and lances visible through the lattice.

dialogue.text: While Jahangir ordered hunts and weighed justice, Mansur continued to work, his studies reflecting a court where curiosity about the natural world stood beside imperial power.

i18n.hi: जहाँ एक तरफ़ जहाँगीर शिकार का हुक्म देता और इंसाफ़ तौलता, वहीं मंसूर लगातार काम करता रहा, उसकी स्टडीज़ एक ऐसे दरबार को दिखाती जहाँ कुदरत की जिज्ञासा, शाही ताक़त के साथ कंधे से कंधा खड़ी थी।

panels.shot: modern museum-like wide, but with period-costume ghostly overlay
panels.action: A dim, gallery-like space shows a framed Mughal bird painting under soft light, while in a ghostly overlay Jahangir and Mansur appear behind it, as if watching from their century.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, such folios lie in distant museums, where scholars use their accuracy to study vanished species and the paths of trade and empire.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद इन्हीं पन्नों को दूर देशों के म्यूज़ियमों में रखा गया, जहाँ उस्ताद उनकी सटीक तस्वीरों से गायब हो चुकी नस्लों और सौदागर‑सल्तनतों के रास्ते तलाशते हैं।

panels.shot: gentle close on Jahangir and Mansur together, looking at a bird in a tree
panels.action: In a quiet garden scene, Jahangir and Mansur stand side by side beneath a tree, both gazing up at a small bird on a branch, the emperor’s face thoughtful, the painter’s hand resting on his folio.

dialogue.text: In their shared work, an emperor’s delight in looking and an artist’s steady hand turned passing wonder into knowledge, leaving traces for ages that would never see those birds alive.

i18n.hi: उनकी साझी मेहनत में, बादशाह की देखने की खुशी और फ़नकार के थामे हुए हाथ ने पल भर की हैरानी को इल्म में बदला, उन ज़मानों के लिए निशान छोड़ दिए जिन्होंने कभी इन पंछियों को ज़िंदा नहीं देखा।

subtitle_i18n.en: In the emperor’s gaze, fleeting wonders become painted memory
subtitle_i18n.hi: बादशाह की नज़र से पल भर का करिश्मा बन गया रंगों में याद
